chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzene is treated with Br2 / FeBr3 catalyst?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzene with Br2 / FeBr3 catalyst yields Bromobenzene + HBr. Rationale: FeBr3 polarizes Br2 into a potent electrophile; attack forms the arenium sigma complex followed by deprotonation.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzene into Nitrobenzene + H2O?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzene into Nitrobenzene + H2O, the appropriate reagent is HNO3 / concentrated H2SO4. Rationale: Sulfuric acid protonates nitric acid to generate the active nitronium ion (NO2+) electrophile.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzene is treated with Fuming H2SO4 (SO3 in H2SO4)?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzene with Fuming H2SO4 (SO3 in H2SO4) yields Benzenesulfonic acid. Rationale: Electrophilic attack of neutral SO3 on benzene yields benzenesulfonic acid; reaction is reversible with steam.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzene into Isopropylbenzene (cumene, major) + Propylbenzene (minor)?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzene into Isopropylbenzene (cumene, major) + Propylbenzene (minor), the appropriate reagent is 1-Chloropropane / AlCl3. Rationale: The primary propyl carbocation-AlCl4 complex rearranges via 1,2-hydride shift to the stable secondary carbocation.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzene is treated with Propanoyl chloride / AlCl3 then H2O?
questions.explanation: Treating Benzene with Propanoyl chloride / AlCl3 then H2O yields 1-Phenyl-1-propanone (propiophenone). Rationale: Acylium ion (CH3CH2C≡O+) is resonance-stabilized and does not undergo skeletal rearrangement.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1-Phenyl-1-propanone into Propylbenzene?
questions.explanation: To convert 1-Phenyl-1-propanone into Propylbenzene, the appropriate reagent is Zn(Hg) / concentrated HCl / heat. Rationale: Amalgamated zinc in strong acid reduces aryl ketones directly to methylene (-CH2-) alkyl chains.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: Which starting material will react with HNO3 / H2SO4 to yield ortho-Nitrotoluene (60%) + para-Nitrotoluene (40%) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Toluene reacts with HNO3 / H2SO4 to yield ortho-Nitrotoluene (60%) + para-Nitrotoluene (40%). Rationale: The methyl group activates the ring through hyperconjugation and directs incoming electrophiles to ortho and para positions.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Nitrobenzene is treated with Cl2 / FeCl3?
questions.explanation: Treating Nitrobenzene with Cl2 / FeCl3 yields meta-Chloronitrobenzene. Rationale: The strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group deactivates all positions, but meta is deactivated least.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) / 100°C then acid to yield 2,4-Dinitrophenol + NaCl as the major product?
questions.explanation: 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene reacts with Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) / 100°C then acid to yield 2,4-Dinitrophenol + NaCl. Rationale: Hydroxide attacks the ipso carbon, forming a resonance-stabilized Meisenheimer complex before expelling chloride.

questions.chapter_title: Chemistry of Benzene: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Chlorobenzene is treated with Sodium amide (NaNH2) in liquid NH3 (-33°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Chlorobenzene with Sodium amide (NaNH2) in liquid NH3 (-33°C) yields Aniline (50% direct + 50% cine substitution). Rationale: Elimination generates the highly strained benzyne intermediate; ammonia attacks both carbons equally.
